title: Refactor legacy GPU loader: timebox startup probes, deterministic symbol blacklist, and dependency debloat
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem:
The current GPU runtime performs an unbounded series of legacy link/probe operations during process startup which increases cold-start latency and causes sporadic startup jitter across mixed node types. Multiple transitive deps (legacy CUDA helpers, optional provider shims, and a catch-all symbol resolver) are contributing to a large resident set size and inconsistent symbol resolution behavior that triggers runtime fallbacks in production.

Goal:
Refactor the legacy loader into a deterministic, timeboxed probe subsystem with a compact dependency surface. Introduce a symbol blacklist/whitelist policy to avoid noisy optional symbol resolution, implement a staged probe timebox that moves noncritical probes to a background warmup path, and provide CI + runtime telemetry to prevent regressions. This should reduce cold-start p50 by ~20-30%, shrink runtime resident size for common images, and remove a class of flakiness seen when multiple CUTLASS/Triton variants are present.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Extract the legacy link/probe logic into a Loader V2 module behind a feature flag (RUNTIME_LOAD_V2).
2) Implement a staged probe timebox: critical probes (required CUDA / cuBLAS / primary kernels) run synchronously with a 150ms budget; noncritical probes (optional optimizations, provider extensions) are scheduled to a background warmup thread with exponential backoff.
3) Introduce a deterministic symbol policy: maintain a compact symbol-blacklist file shipped with runtime that disables known-problem optional symbols, and a whitelist for forced-resolution. Blacklist updates are versioned and signed.
4) Replace ad-hoc dependency enumerations with a dependency manifest parsed at startup to skip known-bloat artifacts.
5) Add a fallback queue that records unresolved optional probes and retries later rather than blocking startup.
6) Add unit/integ tests, CI gating, and canary rollout with telemetry.

Implementation details / trade-offs:
- Synchronous budget: 150ms chosen from perf experiments; can be tuned via env var RUNTIME_PROBE_SYNC_MS. Lowering the budget reduces p50 but may defer useful micro-optimizations to background warmup.
- Blacklist format: newline-delimited symbol names with optional comment lines. Will live in /usr/share/redwood/runtime/symbol_blacklist.txt for on-prem, bundled in image for hosted.
- Signed blacklist: use the existing binary artifact signing flow (ENG-176501) for verification during startup. If signature verification fails, we fall back to embedded fallback blacklist in the runtime binary.
- Background warmup thread: must carefully manage GPU context lifetime; we'll use a single warmed context pool with strict backoff to avoid contention with tenant workloads.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for symbol policy parser and loader state machine.
- Integration tests running mixed model workloads against images containing multiple CUTLASS/Triton variants; assert startup latency delta and verify deterministic symbol behavior.
- Add perf microbenchmarks to CI for cold-start p50 and resident set size.
- Create a staged canary in Dedicated pool (canary-1) then expand to 10% production.

Metrics to track:
- Cold-start p50/p95 latency (Grafana: RT-GPU-Startup-Jitter).
- Runtime RSS median for image variants.
- Number of deferred probes per start.
- Rate of fallback model invocations due to unresolved probes.
- Canary error budget and fallback rates.

Rollout / rollback plan:
- Feature flag off by default. Merge behind RUNTIME_LOAD_V2 flag and enable for internal canary pool.
- After 48 hours and a stable canary, enable for 10% Dedicated traffic. Monitor metrics for 72 hours.
- If regressions > 10% on p95 or > 1% increase in fallback rate, flip flag off and roll back.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Deterministic+Loader+V2+Design
- Perf notes and raw traces: drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LoaderV2Perf (private)
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1987
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/RT-GPU-Startup-Jitter

Next milestones:
- 2025-02-18: land Loader V2 API scaffolding behind feature flag (in progress).
- 2025-02-25: implement symbol policy and background warmup loop.
- 2025-03-04: CI perf gates + canary rollout to internal pool.

Risks / open questions:
- Background warmup may contend with production GPU work if not throttled; need close coordination with scheduler team to respect probe QoS.
- Signature verification dependencies mean we must coordinate with ENG-176501 release cadence.
- Some legacy models rely on late symbol resolution; we need a migration checklist for partner model teams.
